parole.significato: A type of folk theatre from Gujarat.

parole.significato: Buttermilk with added spices.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati ડાંડિયા રાસ (ḍā̃ḍiyā rās).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati ગાંધી (gāndhī, “grocer, merchant”), from Sanskrit गन्ध (gandha, “perfume”). Originally, a trader in perfume.

parole.significato: A person from Gujarat.

parole.significato: One who speaks Gujarati; a Gujarati.

parole.significato: A kind of Gujarati vegetable cake.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati હાંડવો (hā̃ḍvo).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati જાળી (jāḷī, “net”).

parole.significato: An Indian salad of chopped tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, and sometimes chili peppers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati કચુંબર (kacumbar). Doublet of kachumbari.

parole.significato: A Gujarati version of tortilla/crispbread, made with flour, spices, ghee, and lentils.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati ખાખરા (khākhrā) plural of ખાખરો (khākhro).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati ખાંડવી (khā̃ḍvī).

parole.significato: A member of a Gujarati-speaking Shiite sect who take the Aga Khan as their religious head.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati ખોજા (khojā), from Classical Persian خواجه (xwāja), ultimately from Sanskrit उपाध्याय (upādhyāya). Doublet of Ojha, hodja, Hoxha, and Upadhyaya.

parole.significato: The monetary unit of Kutch prior to 1947, divided into 24 dokdas.

parole.significato: To align with the ideology of Narendra Modi or Bharatiya Janata Party.

parole.significato: The ritual through which a person is inducted into the Zoroastrian religion.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati નવજોત (navjot).

parole.significato: A member of a Muslim Rajput community in the state of Gujarat in India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati નાયક (nāyak).

parole.significato: A village head man.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati પટેલ (paṭel, “village headman”), which is from Sanskrit पट्टकिल (paṭṭakila).

parole.significato: A double ikat, usually silk, from Gujarat, western India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati પટોળાં (paṭoḷā̃), plural of પટોળું (paṭoḷũ).

parole.significato: A custom house.
parole.testo: From Gujarati ફુરજો (phurjo), from Arabic فُرْضَة (furḍa).

parole.significato: An animal shelter of a type found almost exclusively in Gujarat.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati પિંજરાપોળ (piñjrāpoḷ).

parole.significato: A philosophy that emphasises socioeconomic equality, non-violence and community development.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati સર્વોદય (sarvodya, “progress of all”), from Sanskrit सर्व (sarva) + उदय (udaya). Coined by Mahatma Gandhi in his Gujarati translation of John Ruskin's Unto This Last.

parole.significato: An Indian snack food consisting of small pieces of crunchy noodles made from chickpea flour paste.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati સેવ (sev).

parole.significato: lake, pond
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati તળાવ (taḷāv) and Marathi तलाव (talāv).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Gujarati ટીંડોરું (ṭī̃ḍorũ).

parole.significato: Synonym of hawala (“informal system of money transfer from India and the Middle East”).

parole.significato: The policy of nonviolent resistance as used by Mahatma Gandhi during the struggle for Indian independence.
parole.testo: Either borrowed from Gujarati સત્યાગ્રહ (satyāgrah) or from Hindi सत्याग्रह (satyāgrah), ultimately from Sanskrit सत्याग्रह (satyāgraha) (in turn, composed of सत्य (satya, “truth”) + आग्रह (āgraha, “persistence”)).
